spmock080.word:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.



A. Climate change

B. to global food security

C. poses

D. according to

E. significant challenges

F. a recent report.
spmock080.explanation:
A. Climate change - This introduces the subject of the sentence, specifying the phenomenon being referred to.

C. poses - This indicates the action or effect caused by climate change, suggesting that it presents challenges or difficulties.

E. significant challenges - This describes the specific impact of climate change, emphasizing that they are substantial or noteworthy challenges.

B. to global food security - This specifies the domain or field to which the challenges are related, indicating that they affect the security or availability of food on a global scale.

D. according to - This introductory phrase indicates the source or reference from which the information is derived.

F. a recent report. - This specifies the specific source of information, namely a report that was recently published.

Therefore, the correct order is ACEBDF.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. 

The rearranged sentence is: Climate change poses significant challenges to global food security, according to a recent report.

spmock080.word:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. 

It is a well-known (A)/ fact that Sameer (B)/ visibly is leading (C)/ the team (D).
spmock080.explanation:
Part C has an error. When the verb phrase has an auxiliary and a main verb, the adverb is placed between the auxiliary and the main verb. In this sentence, the adverb 'possibly' is placed before the auxiliary verb which is incorrect.

The correct sentence is: It is a well-known fact that Sameer is visibly leading the team.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

spmock080.word: Which of the following words can fill in the blank A?
spmock080.explanation:
The blank requires an adjective that defines what type of growth is related to success, as per the narrator. Among the options, 'personal' (belonging to or affecting a particular person rather than anyone else) is the only word that can be attributed to the success of a self. The other options do not convey this meaning and are thus negated.

Provisional- arranged or existing for the present, possibly to be changed later.

Additional- added, extra, or supplementary to what is already present or available.

Provincial- of or concerning a province of a country or empire.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

spmock080.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Mary said to me, "I want to make a complaint about you."
options: Mary tell me that she has wanted to make a complaint about me.
Mary told me that she was wanted to make a complaint about me.
Mary told me that she wanted to make a complaint about me.
Mary told me that she wanted to be made a complaint about me.
spmock080.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject +V1st + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'. 

· The pronouns 'I' and 'you' are changed into 'she' and 'me' respectively. 

· The verb 'want' (present simple) is changed into 'wanted' (past simple).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Mary told me that she wanted to make a complaint about me.

Hence, the answer is option c).

spmock080.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Did the dentist take out your rotten tooth?
options: Was your rotten tooth have been taken out by the dentist?
Has your rotten tooth taken out by the dentist?
Was your rotten tooth taken out by the dentist?
Was your rotten tooth been taken out by the dentist?
spmock080.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like "Did".

The format of the sentence which begins with "Did" in Active voice is: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Was/Were + Subject (Objective case) + V3 + by + Object (Subjective case).

For example:

Did he beat you? (Active)

Were you beaten by him? (Passive)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: (c) Was your rotten tooth taken out by the dentist?

spmock080.word: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition-
options: Apart for English, she is fluent in Spanish and French.

Apart from English, she is fluent in Spanish and French.
Apart of English, she is fluent in Spanish and French.
spmock080.explanation:
Examples of general 'Adverb + Preposition' that are used in general English: Along with, apart from, as for, as to, away from, onto, out of, together with, up to, such as. 

The correct sentence is- Apart from English, she is fluent in Spanish and French.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

options: This year, I have to crack SSC CGL.

SSC CGL has to be cracked by me this year.

·The usage of a helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

·The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

·The question in Active voice is in Infinitive form.

·Infinitive sentence is: To + V1 form.

·The format in Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are/was/were + to + V1 + object

o I have to lend some books. (Active)

spmock080.word:

As far as he is ________, he will love to attend the party.

spmock080.word: Which of the following idioms means 'to be extremely busy or overwhelmed with work or tasks'?

spmock080.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.



A. That city is one of the most important sites of the Indus Civilization, or more accurately, the Harappan Civilization of Pakistan and north-western India.

B. She is one of two bronze artworks found at Mohenjo-Daro that shows a more natural pose than compared to other more formal figures.

C. The Dancing Girl is a bronze statuette created over 4,500 years ago and is a rare and unique masterpiece. 

D. The statuette was named "Dancing Girl" based on an assumption of her profession.
spmock080.explanation:
The correct order is CDBA. 

Sentence C comes first as it introduces us to the main subject of the passage (Dancing Girl bronze statuette). D follows C as it talks about the theory behind the naming of the statuette. So, CD is a pair. Sentence B follows the pair CD and states that the figurine was found in Mohenjo-Daro. A follows B as it talks about this ancient city. 

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

spmock080.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We _________ conform to your demands.
spmock080.explanation:
The blank requires an auxiliary verb phrase that supports the action 'conform' with respect to the noun 'demands'. 'Does/is/was not' correspond to a singular subject, but 'we' is a plural pronoun, so they will be negated. Moreover, 'conform' is in the base form of the verb (V1), so options c) and d) cannot be used and are thus negated. 'Do not' [plural verb] is the most appropriate form of the verb that supports the verb 'conform' as required in the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

The correct sentence is: We do not conform to your demands.

Note:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Verb phrase: A verb phrase is the verbal part of a clause. A verb phrase has an ordinary verb (come, thought, left, climbing) and may also have an auxiliary verb (had, was, will) Example: She had already thought about the idea before. Here 'thought' is the main verb, 'had' the auxiliary verb and the highlighted part, the verb phrase.

spmock081.word:

Albert is intemperate, irresolute, and unreflective - and he makes bad decisions and develops bad habits.
spmock081.explanation:
Tenacious - not readily relinquishing a position, principle, or course of action; determined.

Irresolute - showing or feeling hesitancy; uncertain; not able or willing to take decisions or actions.

Both words are opposite in meaning. Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Develops - grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.

Decisions - a conclusion or resolution reached after consideration.

Intemperate - having or showing a lack of self-control; immoderate.

spmock081.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Rustom told me that when he asked her about the truth, she wasn't responding.
options: Rustom said to me, "When I had asked her about the truth, she wasn't responding."
Rustom said to me, "When I asked her about the truth, she wasn't responding."

spmock081.explanation:
If the sentence is in the Past tense, the form of tense doesn't change when it is used in the time clause.

One way of identifying the time clause is that the Time clause always begins with the following:WhenWheneverWhileAsSinceAfterBeforeUntilAs soon as

For example:

spmock081.word: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.

NOTE:

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

spmock083.word:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

A large amount of people were protesting against the new policy on taxation.
options: A large amount of people was protesting against the new policy on taxation.
A large number of people was protesting against the new policy on taxation.
A large number of people were protesting against the new policy on taxation.
A large amount of people were protest against the new policy on taxation.
spmock083.explanation:
The error in the original sentence lies in the use of the quantifier "amount of" with the noun "people".

The choice between "amount" and "number" depends on whether the noun is countable or uncountable.

"Amount of" is used with uncountable nouns (things that cannot be counted individually, like water, sugar, information, or time).

"Number of" is used with countable nouns (things that can be counted individually, like books, cars, or people).

In the sentence, "people" is a countable noun. Therefore, using "A large amount of" is incorrect. The correct phrase is "A large number of".

So, options (a) and (d) are incorrect as they use the phrase "a large amount of". 

The phrase "A number of..." is considered a plural subject and takes a plural verb.

"A large number of people" (plural subject) requires a plural verb.

Option b): This is incorrect. Although it correctly uses "number", it uses the singular verb "was" instead of the required plural verb "were".

Option c): This is correct. It uses the correct quantifier "number" for the countable noun "people" and the correct plural verb "were".

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. 

Note: Quantifier: A word or phrase that is used before a noun to show the amount of it that is being considered: "Some", "many", "a lot of", and "a few" are examples of quantifiers.

Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table'  -  one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

spmock083.word: Describe how you will say to your colleague You are wanted by the manager in active voice.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

spmock083.word:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. 

Neither the manager nor the assistant manager were available when the client arrived for the meeting.

The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'were available when the'. The error is related to subject-verb agreement. The subject of the sentence is "Neither the manager nor the assistant manager." This is a compound subject connected to "neither...nor." When using "neither...nor," the verb should agree with the closer subject in terms of proximity. In this case, "assistant manager" is closer to the verb. "Assistant manager" is a singular subject, so the verb should be singular as well. The correct verb form to use with a singular subject is "was" [singular] not "were" [plural]. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 

The correct sentence is: Neither the manager nor the assistant manager was available when the client arrived for the meeting.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb. 

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live  -  lives.

spmock083.word:

R) that fosters a community 

S) where people are embraced 

regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.

It describes what happens as a consequence of embracing acceptance, which is the development of a culture characterised by openness and tolerance. Part R connects to the previous part by explaining the purpose or impact of the culture of openness and tolerance mentioned earlier. It states that this culture serves as a foundation or environment that supports the creation or development of a community. Parts S and Q further explain the nature of the community. They describe that in the community, people are welcomed or accepted for who they are. This implies that people are accepted as it is, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity. The correct sequence (PRSQ) maintains a logical flow in the sentence structure by first introducing the result of embracing acceptance (cultivating openness and tolerance), explaining how this culture fosters a community, and finally describing the inclusive nature of that community where individuals are embraced regardless of their background or beliefs. This arrangement forms a coherent and meaningful sentence describing the positive effects of embracing acceptance. 

The sentence formed is: Embracing acceptance cultivates a culture of openness and tolerance that fosters a community where people are embraced for who they are, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Since Monday, I am trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages.

'Since' is a time expression that denotes a point of time.

The rule is: Present Indefinite + Time expression= Present Perfect.

For example: Monika has known me since 1995.

Similarly, in this question, 'Since' is a time expression. So, 'am trying' must be replaced by 'have been trying' (present perfect tense) in the sentence.

Additional Information:

'Since' denotes a period of time.

spmock084.word: Describe how you will say The challan shall be filled by the attendee in active voice.
options: The attendee shall be fill the challan.
The attendee shall fill the challan.
The attendee shall be filling the challan.
spmock084.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb 'be' and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

spmock085.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form.

We received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
options: We will be receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We have received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We had received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
We were receiving a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.
spmock085.explanation:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in present tense form is (b). Option (b) changes the verb "received" (past tense) to "have received" (present perfect tense). The present perfect tense is used to talk about actions that were completed at some unspecified time before the present moment and have relevance to the present. It is formed using the auxiliary verb "have" (or "has" for singular subjects) followed by the past participle of the main verb (in this case, "received"). Option (a) is in the future continuous tense ("will be" + present participle of the verb). Option (c) is in the past perfect tense ("had" + past participle of the verb). Option (d) is in the past continuous tense ("were"/ "was" + present participle of the verb). Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

The other options do not fit:

· "and" would illogically suggest both are equally valued in the same way, contradicting the "not" at the beginning.

· "so" introduces a result, which does not fit the corrective structure of the sentence.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "The company values his contribution, not for his experience, but for his innovative mindset."

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Note: A conjunction (also called a connective) is a word such as and, because, but, for, if, or, when etc. Conjunctions are used to connect phrases, clauses, and sentences.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

spmock087.word:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence. 

Having being in the company(A)/ for over a decade, / Michael was well-versed in(B)/ the intricacies of the industry/ and had developed strong(C)/ relationships with clients. / No error (D).
spmock087.explanation:
"Having" is a gerund or present participle form of the verb "have," which is used to indicate an ongoing action or state. However, in this context, we need the past participle form of the verb.

"Being" is the present participle, which is used in continuous tenses (e.g., "is being," "was being"), and it's inappropriate here because the sentence refers to a past and completed action.

"Having been" is the correct past perfect participle form, used to indicate a completed action in the past that is relevant to the present or another past event. In this sentence, it implies that Michael's long presence in the company led to his expertise and relationships.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence: Having been in the company for over a decade, Michael was well-versed in the intricacies of the industry and had developed strong relationships with clients.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Option 4 uses the first conditional ("If + present simple, will + base verb"), which is correct for describing a likely future outcome based on a present condition. The structure is "If you work hard" (present simple) followed by "you will achieve success" (future simple).

spmock087.word: Select a grammatically correct sentence using the future tense.

The correct option is b) As soon as the sun sets, the streetlights will turn on automatically.

This sentence demonstrates the correct structure for future time clauses. When a clause begins with a time conjunction like "as soon as," "when," "before," or "after" and refers to the future, it must use the simple present tense ("sets"). The main clause then uses the simple future tense ("will turn on").

Let's look at why the other options are incorrect:

· Option (a): This is incorrect because the future tense ("will set") cannot be used in a future time clause starting with "as soon as".

· Option (c): This has two errors: it incorrectly uses the future tense in the time clause and uses the present continuous tense ("are turning on") in the main clause, which is less appropriate than the simple future for a statement of future fact.

· Option (d): This has two errors: it incorrectly uses the present perfect ("has set") in the time clause and "would" instead of "will" in the main clause.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech. If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

I. Tense remains the same.

II. Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

III. Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3+Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had+ V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech). Here, case 3 will be used, as per the options.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Reporting verb 'enquired' changed to 'asked me'.

The verb phrase 'I had gone' changed to 'Did you go'.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

The correct verb must be plural. "Sit" is the correct plural verb in the present tense.

· Option b) "sat two beautiful, chirping bird" incorrectly uses the singular noun "bird" with the number "two." It should be "birds."

· Option d) "sits two beautiful, chirping bird" is incorrect as it uses the singular verb "sits" and the singular noun "bird."

So, the correct sentence is: Just before sunrise, there on the highest branch of the old banyan tree, sit two beautiful, chirping birds.

spmock091.word: Select the appropriate word to fill blank C.

The verb has to be either in Past participle form (V3) or continuous/present participle form (V4) to be used along with the auxiliary verb 'are'. 'Reward' and 'expect' are in base forms of the verbs (V1), so they are negated. Note:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. spmock092.explanation:

"The best dancer" is correct because "best" is a superlative adjective. A superlative adjective shall be followed by the definite article "the". And "a talented performer" is correct because "talented" starts with a consonant sound and aptly follows the indefinite article "a". This is because "a" is used before consonant-sounding words.

B: Incorrect

"A best dancer" is incorrect because "best" is a superlative, and superlatives should be used with "the." "A talented performer" is correct.

C: Incorrect

"The best dancer" is correct, but "in competition" should be "in the competition" to specify a particular competition. "A talented performer" is correct.

D: Incorrect

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

John said, "I was studying for the exam last evening."

John said that he had been studying for the exam the previous evening.
spmock092.explanation:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had + been + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I was watching television last night." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had been watching television the previous night. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said' is changed to 'said that'.

'I' is changed to 'he'.

'Was' is changed to 'had been'.

'Last evening' is changed to 'the previous night'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: John said that he had been studying for the exam the previous evening.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The island is / surround by/ sharks and / rare marine creatures.

Accordingly, the past participle form of the verb 'surrounded' is to be used instead of 'surround' since the sentence is in the passive voice. The subject 'island' is what the action 'surrounded' is subjected to.

The correct sentence is: The island is surrounded by sharks and rare marine creatures.

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Note:

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Note: In English grammar, "attributive" and "predicative" refer to the positions of adjectives in relation to nouns. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

spmock095.word:

Who can transfer the money to any account in India?
Who could transfer the money to any account in India?
Who transfers the money to any account in India?
spmock095.explanation:
The correct answer is option b).

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from passive to active. There is no change in the tense.

The following syntax is used for the above sentence:-

Passive voice- By whom + can + object + be + V3

Active voice- Who(subject) + can + V1 + object

spmock095.word:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My father give up/smoking when/I was twelve / years old.

'Father' is a singular noun which cannot be followed by the plural verb 'gives'. Also, 'when I was twelve years old' implies that the father stopped smoking in the past.

So, 'give' should be replaced with the past tense form of the verb, i.e., 'gave'.

The correct sentence is: My father gave up smoking when I was twelve years old.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

spmock095.word:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Football fans are feeling proud of their teams when they win.

spmock095.explanation:
The given sentence does not describe a situation that is happening at present. So, the use of 'are feeling' (present continuous tense) is incorrect. Option (d) is incorrect for the same reason.

'Proud' will be followed by 'of'. So, option (a) is incorrect as well.

'Are' should be followed by either past participle (V3) or present participle (V4), none of which is a case in option (c). So, option (c) is incorrect as well.

Replacing the underlined segment with option (b) will make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct.

The correct sentence is: Football fans feel proud of their teams when they win.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

spmock095.word: Identify the active voice usage in the sentences below.
options: The movie was watched by a large audience last night.
The new software update was installed on all computers.
The secret formula was stolen by an unknown intruder.
The chef prepared a gourmet meal for the VIP guests.
spmock095.explanation:
In option (d), the subject is "the chef," the verb is "prepared," and the object is "a gourmet meal for the VIP guests." To determine if the sentence is in the active voice, we need to check if the subject is performing the action.

Here, the subject ("the chef") is indeed performing the action of preparing the meal. The sentence is structured in a way that clearly shows the doer of the action ("the chef"). Therefore, this sentence is in the active voice.

In the active voice, the subject is the one who performs the action, and the structure of the sentence usually follows the pattern: Subject + Verb + Object. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Other options are in the passive voice.

spmock095.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Access denied.
options: Let it be known that access will be denied.
spmock095.explanation:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The question in Active voice is in the imperative form. An imperative sentence is used to express order, request, suggestion, etc. They begin with a principal verb. Here, the imperative sentence in Active voice is an order.

The format in Active voice is: V1 + Object.

Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: Let + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + be + V3.

For example:

Start the match. (Active)

Let the match be started. (Passive)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Let the access be denied.

spmock095.word:
A sentence has been split up into segments and given below in jumbled order. While the first and the last segments of the sentence (1 and 6) are in the correct order, the segments in between are jumbled up. Arrange the segments in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

P) and the learned man has been held in higher esteem

6) than the warrior or the administrator.
spmock095.explanation:
The sentence starts with "India has been a land" and ends with "than the warrior or the administrator." The middle segments must describe India's relationship with learning. Starting with Q, "of learning through the ages," defines the land. Then, S, "not indeed in the sense that education has been universal," clarifies the nature of learning. Next, R, "but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued," contrasts with S. Finally, P, "and the learned man has been held in higher esteem," connects to the ending.

The order Q-S-R-P forms: "India has been a land of learning through the ages, not indeed in the sense that education has been universal, but in the sense that learning has always been very highly valued, and the learned man has been held in higher esteem than the warrior or the administrator."

Option 2 is correct.

spmock095.word:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Me and my colleague have decided / to take up the challenging new project / offered by the senior management team.
options: Me and my colleague have decided
to take up the challenging new project
offered by the senior management team
spmock095.explanation:
The error is in the part "Me and my colleague have decided". When a pronoun is part of a compound subject (performing the action of the verb "have decided"), the subjective case of the pronoun should be used. "Me" is an objective pronoun. The correct subjective pronoun is "I". Also, it is conventional to place the pronoun "I" after other nouns or pronouns in a compound subject.

Correct Sentence: My colleague and I have decided to take up the challenging new project offered by the senior management team.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party. "I" is the correct subjective pronoun here.

· Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions. "Me" is incorrectly used as a subject.

spmock095.word:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with one blank, followed by four options, each having a word which may or may not fit in the blank. From the given options, choose the one that gives the correct word that fits in the blank.

The error is in the use of the preposition "on" after "angry." When one is angry with a person, the correct preposition to use is "with." The preposition "at" is used when one is angry about a thing or a situation. Since the father is angry with a person ("me"), "with" should be used.

Correct sentence: My father was very angry with me for breaking his favourite expensive vase while playing cricket inside.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

spmock095.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She behaves ________ she were the queen of the entire world.
spmock095.explanation:
The sentence describes someone's behaviour by comparing it to an unreal or hypothetical situation. The use of "were" (subjunctive mood) indicates that the situation is imaginary - she is not actually the queen. The blank requires a conjunction that can introduce such a hypothetical or unreal comparison.

The correct option is "as if". This conjunction is used to talk about an imaginary situation or a situation that may not be true. It is correctly paired with the subjunctive mood ("were") to describe her behaviour.

The other options do not fit:

· "like" is often used informally in this way, but in formal grammar, "as if" or "as though" is preferred before a clause (a group of words with a subject and a verb).

· "since" gives a reason or indicates a point in time.

· "when" refers to a specific time.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "She behaves as if she were the queen of the entire world."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note: A conjunction (also called a connective) is a word such as and, because, but, for, if, or, when etc. Conjunctions are used to connect phrases, clauses, and sentences.

spmock095.word:

spmock096.word:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. 

Personal growth (transforming) lives profoundly.
spmock096.explanation:
'Transforming' (-ing form of verb) requires a helping verb before it which is absent in the given sentence.

Options (a) and (b) are incorrect as the verb following the helping verbs 'was' and 'is' should either be a past participle (V3) or a present participle verb (V4, i.e., the -ing form of the verb), but 'transform' is a base verb.

Option (c) correctly uses the singular present tense verb "transforms," which agrees with the singular subject "personal growth." This choice effectively conveys the idea that personal growth is an ongoing process that has a profound impact on lives. It is the most suitable choice as it maintains subject-verb agreement. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: Personal growth transforms lives profoundly.

The rest of the options form grammatically incorrect sentences.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

A participle is a word derived from a verb that can be used as an adjective or to form certain verb tenses. There are two main types of participles:



Past participles (typically ending in -ed, -en, -n, -ne, or -t) are used for perfect tenses and passive voice constructions.

Present participles (always ending in -ing) are used for continuous tenses.

spmock096.word:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.

spmock096.explanation:
The most appropriate word to fill in the blank is 'whose'. The given sentence/blank requires a word that connects the man to the book he owns or is associated with. The word "whose" is a relative pronoun that is used to indicate possession or ownership. In the given context, it effectively connects the man to the book he owns. It indicates that the book belongs to the man. The word "who" is used to refer to a person, but it doesn't convey possession or ownership. It simply identifies the person. The relative pronoun "whom" also doesn't convey possession or ownership. "That" is a relative pronoun used to refer to people or things, but it doesn't convey possession or ownership. It simply identifies the person or thing being referred to. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 

The complete sentence is: The man whose book you are reading is my father.

NOTE:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

spmock096.word:

spmock096.word: Select the option with the correct use of the present tense.

The Earth has been revolving around the Sun since an elliptical orbit.
spmock096.explanation:
The correct option is b) The Earth revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit.

This sentence correctly uses the simple present tense (revolves). The simple present tense is used to state universal truths, scientific facts, and general habits that are always true. The fact that the Earth orbits the Sun is a universal truth.

Let's look at why the other options are incorrect:

· Option (a): This uses the present continuous tense ("is revolving"). This tense is used for actions happening right now or for temporary situations, not for permanent universal truths.

· Option (c): This uses the present perfect tense ("has revolved"), which implies a recently completed action or an action with a result in the present. This is inappropriate for a timeless fact.

· Option (d): This uses the present perfect continuous tense incorrectly. "Since" must be followed by a point in time, not a description of the orbit like "an elliptical orbit".

Note:

"Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Option a) 'a very useful piece of advice' correctly uses the countable phrase 'a piece of' to refer to a single instance of the uncountable noun 'advice'.

Option b) 'some very useful advices' is incorrect because 'advice' does not have a plural form 'advices'.

Option c) 'a very useful advise' is incorrect for two reasons: it uses the article 'a' with an uncountable noun, and 'advise' (with an 's') is a verb, not a noun.

Option d) 'No substitution' is incorrect because the original phrase is grammatically flawed.

The correct sentence is: My father gave me a very useful piece of advice before I left for my first job interview, telling me to be confident, honest, and to listen carefully to every question asked.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Note:

Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table'  -  one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

spmock098.word: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
options: A scientist will has presented a theory at an important conference.

spmock098.explanation:
Option (a) is incorrect because "will has presented" is grammatically wrong. The correct form would be "will have presented" if using the future perfect tense as "will" should be followed by the base form of the verb "have". 

Option (b) is incorrect because "will have present" is not grammatically correct. In the future perfect tense, the verb should be in the past participle form [third form of verb], i.e., "will have presented."

Option (c) is correct because "will present" is the correct use of the simple future tense to indicate an action that will occur in the future.

Option (d) is incorrect because "will presents" is not a valid verb form. After "will," the base form of the verb ("present") is required.

Hence, option (c) is the answer. 

Note: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

Note:

· The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

spmock099.word: Select the option that is expressed in passive voice.
options: The joy it brought me is immeasurable.
The delays in appointments are not something we can afford.
I was awarded the National Florence Nightingale Award for meritorious service in nursing.
Adequate and appropriate training of medical and paramedical staff is critical.
spmock099.explanation:
When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Only in option c), the subject "I" is what the action is directed at.

The passive voice in option (c) is in the Past Indefinite tense.

In Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

The correct sentence would be: Measles is a highly contagious virus that lives in the nose and throat mucus of an infected person.

spmock101.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Between the red shirt and the blue one, I like the _________ more.
spmock101.explanation:
The sentence presents two options ("the red shirt and the blue one") and expresses a preference for the second one mentioned. The blank requires an adjective that refers to the second of two things.

The rule tested is the difference between "latter" and "later."

The correct option is "latter," which specifically refers to the second of two people or things just mentioned.

The other options are incorrect: "later" refers to a point in time. "Last" is used when there are more than two items in a list. "Latest" means the most recent.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "Between the red shirt and the blue one, I like the latter more."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

spmock101.word:

Hence, (d) is correct.

spmock101.word:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The helicopter of the enemies / hovered exact / over their bunker.
spmock101.explanation:
The verb 'hovered' requires an adverb after it to modify/qualify it, whereas 'exact' is an adjective/verb. It needs to be replaced with the adverb 'exactly'.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

spmock101.word:

Pulled off - succeed in achieving or winning something difficult.

Pulled down - demolish a building.

Filling the blank with 'pulled down' makes the sentence contextually correct as it implies that the old building was demolished by the authorities. 

Other options do not fit in contextually. 

The correct sentence is: The old building was pulled down by the authorities.

Learn more and you'll generate ideas and enthusiasm for ____ other changes.

The idiom 'forty winks' means 'a short sleep, especially during the day'.

Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Praise someone openly: Incorrect, as the idiom refers to undermining someone, not giving them praise.

Help someone succeed: Incorrect, as the idiom implies taking away someone's recognition, not aiding them.

Keep a secret: Incorrect, as the idiom has nothing to do with confidentiality.

spmock101.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.



A. To compensate for this change in lifestyle we need physical exercise.

B. Our society is turning towards more and more technical sophistication and automation. 

C. It keeps a balance between our body and mind. 

D. However, over-exercise or exercising in an improper way may tell upon our health and growth.
spmock101.explanation:
Sentence B comes first as it is an independent sentence and provides a platform to carry forward the discussion. A follows B as it talks about what should we do to compensate for this change into automation. Sentence A states that we should exercise, and C follows A as it talks about what we can achieve by doing physical exercise. 'However' is used to show a contrast with something that had been said before. D follows C as it contrasts sentence C. Therefore, BACD becomes the correct order among the given options. 

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

spmock101.word:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order. 

P. The cinematic effects in her 

Q. Of the past

R. The great filmmakers 

S. Films are clearly borrowed from
spmock101.explanation:
The correct order to form a meaningful sentence is PSRQ. Part P comes first as it introduces the subject of the sentence, which is "The cinematic effects" (it indicates that cinematic effect is present in something). Part S then specifies what the cinematic effects are related to (Films). It states that cinematic effects are present in her films. It also indicates that these cinematic effects are borrowed. Part R further introduces the individuals from whom the cinematic effects are borrowed (filmmakers). Accordingly, SR forms a necessary pair. Part Q then qualifies the time period or era from which these great filmmakers are from, indicating they are historical figures. Hence, (d) is the correct answer. 

The complete sentence is: The cinematic effects in her films are clearly borrowed from the great filmmakers of the past.

spmock101.word:
Identify the pair of synonyms from the underlined words in the given sentence. 

Despite the personal cost, perfectionists believe that treating themselves harshly is necessary because if they let up an inch, they'll never achieve anything, and they'll earn the scorn or disappointment of others.
spmock101.explanation:
Cost- the effort, loss, or sacrifice necessary to achieve or obtain something

Scorn- a feeling and expression of contempt or disdain for someone or something

Harshly- in a manner that is unpleasantly rough or jarring to the senses

Anything- used to refer to a thing, no matter what

Achieve- successfully bring about or reach (a desired objective or result) by effort, skill, or courage

Earn- gain deservedly in return for one's behaviour or achievements

Personal- belonging to or affecting a particular person rather than anyone else

Necessary- needed to be done, achieved, or present; essential

Among the underlined words, only 'achieve' and 'earn' are synonymous with each other and so, they are the required pair of synonyms from the underlined words.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

spmock101.word:

I need to buy ____ tickets for the concert next weekend.

Too - "Too" is an adverb that means "also" or "excessively." 

To - "To" is a preposition or part of an infinitive verb. 

Toe - "Toe" refers to one of the five digits on the foot.

spmock101.word:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Remembrance

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

spmock101.word:
In the question given below, a part of the sentence is bracketed. Below the sentence, are given alternatives to the bracketed part which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is required, choose 'No Improvement' option.

(As soon as he was) gone than Lisa unlocked the door.

spmock102.word:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

My father is / an honest man and / always speaks the truth to everyone.
options: always speaks the truth to everyone
spmock102.explanation:
The sentence is grammatically correct. The indefinite article "an" is correctly used before "honest" because "honest" begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent).

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

spmock102.word:
Fill in the blank with the verb in the Future Perfect Tense. 

The teacher ____ our answer books.
spmock102.explanation:
The format of Future Perfect Tense is  -  Subject + will + have + V3 (past participle). Hence, (a) is the correct answer. 

The final sentence would be: The teacher will have marked our answer books.

spmock102.word:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After hearing their explanation,/ we understood that/ they had knew the/ consequences of their actions.
spmock102.explanation:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is "they had knew the". 

The error is related to the past tense verb "knew." The correct form should be "known," which is the past participle form of "know" (knew is the past tense form). 

In the past perfect tense, the helping verb "had" is followed by the past participle form of the main verb (not by the past tense form). 

Therefore, the correct phrase should be "they had known," not "they had knew." Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: After hearing their explanation, we understood that they had known the consequences of their actions.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

spmock102.word:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The manager said that / my project was / more unique than all / the other submissions.
spmock102.explanation:
The error is in using a comparative form with an absolute adjective. Adjectives like "unique", "perfect", "extreme", "complete", and "absolute" describe states that cannot be graded. Something is either unique or it is not; it cannot be "more unique". Such adjectives do not have comparative or superlative forms.

Note: Absolute adjectives (or non-gradable adjectives) represent an absolute quality. Therefore, adding comparatives like 'more' or superlatives like 'most' to them is grammatically incorrect.

Correct sentence: The manager said that my project was unique among all the other submissions.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

The queen's palace is far away with my house.
spmock102.explanation:
In the underlined part, the preposition 'with' which means 'accompanied by' is a contextually incorrect preposition as the word needs to indicate the distance of the palace from the point of reference (my house). Accordingly, option (c) 'away from' is the most appropriate option in which the preposition 'from' (indicating the distance between a particular place and another place used as a point of reference) is the ideal word to match the context of the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party. 

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence.

His brother _______ his _______ and gave him a watch after his result.
spmock102.explanation:
Among the given options, the option with the words 'kept' and 'promise' is the most appropriate choice. The phrase 'keep a promise' means 'to do what you said you would do'. The latter part of the sentence confirms that he gave his watch to keep his promise.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

spmock102.word:
In the following passage, a word has been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Manpower exporters and overseas recruiter's commonly________ in illegal business practices for short-term______ gain.
spmock102.explanation:
The given sentence mentions a few exporters and recruiters related with illegal business practices. The first blank would represent the action by the subject 'exporters and recruiters' with respect to illegal business practices. So, 'honoured' will not fit in contextually. Hence, option (a) is negated.

The verb 'regulated' requires the object to denote what is controlled by the subject, which is absent in the given sentence. So, option (c) is incorrect as well.

'Devotional gain' and 'illegal business practices' have no relation. So, option (d) is incorrect as well.

Filling the blanks with 'indulged' (means 'to take unrestrained pleasure in') and 'monetary' (means 'of or relating to money') gives the meaning that such people engage in illegal practices to earn money illegally.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

The correct sentence is: Manpower exporters and overseas recruiters commonly indulged in illegal business practices for short-term monetary gain.

spmock102.word:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.

It was a great priviledge to meet the esteemed guest speaker today.
spmock102.explanation:
The incorrectly spelt word is priviledge. The correct spelling is privilege, which means a special right, advantage, or immunity granted or available only to a particular person or group.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

Ruby gave her mother a hug and offered to knead the ________.
spmock102.explanation:
· The sentence refers to kneading, which is an action related to dough made from flour.

· Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings.

· Flour (correct choice) → Fine powder used for baking.

· Flora → Refers to plant life, incorrect in this context.

· Flavour → Taste of food, unrelated to kneading.

· Floor → The bottom surface of a room, incorrect here.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence.

This new pair of (scissor is extremely sharp) and must be handled carefully.
spmock102.explanation:
The error in the bracketed segment is the word 'scissor'. The noun for the cutting tool is 'scissors', which is always plural. However, the subject of the sentence is the singular phrase 'This new pair'. Therefore, the verb must be singular ('is') to agree with 'pair'.

· Option a) 'scissors are extremely sharp' uses the correct noun but the incorrect plural verb 'are'. The verb should agree with 'pair', not 'scissors'.

· Option b) 'scissors is extremely sharp' correctly uses the noun 'scissors' and the singular verb 'is' (which agrees with the subject 'pair').

· Option c) 'scissor are extremely sharp' has two errors: the incorrect noun 'scissor' and the incorrect plural verb 'are'.

· Option d) 'scissor's is extremely sharp' incorrectly uses a possessive form of the wrong noun.

The correct sentence is: This new pair of scissors is extremely sharp and must be handled carefully.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

spmock102.word: What is the author's tone in this passage?
spmock102.explanation:
The author's tone is concerned, as the passage highlights the serious issues of forest encroachment, wildlife threats, and the near-endangered status of the Black Buck. The author expresses worry about the extinction of species, stating, "Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction," and notes the adverse effects of hunting despite conservation efforts: "Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife." The suggestion to boycott products and the rhetorical question, "This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That's a question," further indicate a tone of concern about the future of wildlife.

(a) Revengeful: A revengeful tone would imply a desire for retaliation or vengeance, which is absent. The author does not express anger or a call for punishment but focuses on concern and solutions (e.g., boycotting products).

(b) Impressed: An impressed tone would suggest admiration or approval, which is inappropriate given the passage's focus on negative issues like extinction and poaching, not positive achievements.

(c) Agitated: An agitated tone implies intense anger or restlessness, but the passage maintains a measured, informative style, expressing worry rather than outrage, as seen in the calm proposal of solutions.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4).

spmock102.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The contract will have been signed by the partners by next Friday.
options: The partners will have signed the contract by next Friday.
The partners will sign the contract by next Friday.
The partners will be signing the contract by next Friday.
The partners would sign the contract by next Friday.
spmock102.explanation:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb (been) and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

For example:

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The partners will have signed the contract by next Friday.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

spmock102.word:
Given below is a four-sentence paragraph (S1-S4). S1 and S4 are given. From the options (P, Q, R) choose two sentences which can be S2 and S3.

S1: Painite is the second-rarest mineral in existence, which appears as deep red hexagonal crystals.

S2: ___________________________

S3: ___________________________

S4: But unbeknownst to Pain, they were actually something far rarer.

P. In 1952, the English gem collector and dealer Arthur Pain acquired two crimson crystals in Myanmar.

Q. The very first painite crystal discovered, known as painite #1, was later analyzed by Rossman.

R. Pain thought the crystals were rubies, which the region is famed for.
spmock102.explanation:
S1 introduces us to the painite crystal which is the second-rarest mineral on earth. P states that in 1952 Arthur Pain acquired two crimson crystals in Myanmar. R follows P as it states that Pain thought that those two crystals were rubies. 'But' is used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned. S4 states that those were not rubies but actually a far rarer mineral. Sentence Q does not fit in as it tells about another person, Rossman, whereas sentence S4 talks about someone by the name of 'Pain'. 

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

spmock102.word:
Select the appropriate preposition for the given blanks.

Select the appropriate option for the given blank-

She was admitted to his office immediately _____ her arrival.
spmock102.explanation:
'Upon' is used to show that something happens soon after, and often because of, something else. 

The correct sentence is- She was admitted to his office immediately upon her arrival.

Hence, option (c) is correct. 

To - to indicate a destination or direction.

Among - situated more or less centrally in relation to (several other things).

For - used to indicate the place someone or something is going to or toward.

In - expressing the situation of something that is or appears to be enclosed or surrounded by something else.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold.

His mother never held a grudge against his father.

spmock102.word:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The decision was made among the two parties so we can say that it was a mutual decision.
options: so we can say that it
spmock102.explanation:
As per rule-

a) Between is used when we talk about two persons or things. 

Example: Between red and yellow, I will prefer red. 

b) Among is used when we talk about more than two persons or things. 

Example: Please choose one among the five options. 

The correct is- The decision was made between the two parties so we can say that it was a mutual decision.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

spmock102.word:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Bite off more than you can chew
options: He bit off more than he could chew when he ordered a large pizza and could finish it.

I bit off more than I could chew when I decided to try a new restaurant.
They bit off more than they could chew when they ate too many candies at the party.
spmock102.explanation:
The idiom "bite off more than you can chew" means to take on more responsibilities or tasks than one can handle. It implies overestimating one's capacity or ability to manage a situation. Among the given options, option (b) correctly uses the idiom to describe taking on multiple projects and struggling to complete them. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The rest of the options use the idiom incorrectly.

spmock102.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.



The girl told her friends that she had taken her little brother to walk in the garden.
options: The girl said to her friends, "I am taking my little brother to walk in the garden."
The girl said to her friends, "I took my little brother to walk in the garden."
The girl said to her friends, "She took the garden to walk in my little brother."
The girl said to her friends, "She has been taken my little brother to walk in the garden."
spmock102.explanation:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Simple or Present Perfect tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

OR

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

The first case is applicable here (past simple).

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The reporting verb 'told' is changed into 'said to'.

· The pronoun 'she' is changed into 'I'.

· The possessive determiner 'her' is changed into 'my'.

· Verb 'Had taken' is changed into 'took'.

Option (a) is eliminated because it is in present continuous tense. Option (c) is eliminated because the meaning of the sentence has been changed. Option (d) is eliminated because the verb is in passive voice which is contextually incorrect in this case.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The girl said to her friends, "I took my little brother to walk in the garden."

spmock102.word:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.

What are you looking around?
spmock102.explanation:
The correct phrasal verb in this context is "look for," which means "to search for something." 

Other options are incorrect because:

· "Look among" is incorrect because "among" is used for selecting from a group.

· "Look across" means to glance over something.

· "Look through" means to examine something carefully.

spmock102.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This is the ______ book that I have read till now.
spmock102.explanation:
It can be noted that the sentence is in the superlative degree, signifying that the book that is mentioned in the sentence is ultimate amongst all the books the subject has read so far. So, the superlative adjective "most interesting" is appropriate for comparing the book to all others read, indicating it is the best in terms of interest.

The complete sentence: This is the most interesting book that I have read till now.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.
